# GitHub Copilot

Enable **GitHub Copilot** in **Settings > Providers** on the environment running
your project. It uses the native Copilot SDK and your existing Copilot account,
not the ACP registry or a separately billed hosted model service.

Sign in on that environment with `copilot login`, then refresh provider status.
Models and reasoning options come from your account's available catalog.

**Hide internal models** is off by default. Enable it in this provider's settings
to exclude account models labelled `internal only` from model pickers. Explicit
custom models remain available.

When **Auto** is available in your model catalog, you can select it to let Copilot
choose the model using its current routing preferences. Auto remains available
even when the account does not supply routing-preference details.

When your account advertises routing preferences, Auto's **Routing** option includes the
eligible preferences, including Fusion. Disabled preferences show their account-specific reason.
Requests can remain pending before they take effect; the activity log distinguishes requested,
effective, and activating routing and shows reported model phases and timing. See
[Activity log](activity-log.md). Explicit-model selection and defaults are unchanged.

To opt in to dynamic Fusion tiers, turn on **Enable Fusion** for this provider in
**Settings > Providers**. The setting is off by default on each environment.
Changing an explicit routing preference renews the Copilot runtime and resumes
the same native conversation, so existing chats receive the updated setting.
When the account advertises Fusion, the model
picker shows **Fusion**, with a separate **Fusion effort** control for its available
tiers, such as **Standard**, **High**, and **Max**. Names and availability come from
your account; choosing an effort does not pin the solver or reviewer model.

Choose **Provider default** in the effort control to explicitly clear a saved
preference. Omitting a preference on reconnect instead restores the committed
selection. A change may remain pending until the next turn.

Background generation, including titles and source-control text, honors the
selected account-advertised routing preference. Unavailable preferences fail
explicitly rather than silently using a different tier.

Fusion can use one model or multiple draft/review phases. The activity log shows
reported phases and the final source model, while chat shows the committed final
answer rather than intermediate drafts. Fusion-enabled Auto answers appear as full
responses; ordinary model streaming remains available.

The default runtime uses the bundled Copilot executable. **Binary path** can
override it. **COPILOT_HOME path** selects the account's configuration and native
session directory; separate provider instances can use separate directories.
Configuration, credentials, and sessions stay on the environment, including when
you connect from the web app, desktop, or mobile.

## Project configuration and skills

**Discover project configuration** loads the project's native MCP servers,
instructions, and skills. The skill picker uses the current project's discovered
skills, not a combined list from unrelated projects. Disabled and agent-only
skills are not offered as user commands.
The picker does not currently expose enable/disable controls.

## Conversations and permissions

Native conversations resume after reconnecting. If another client already owns a
native session, T3 Code refuses to take it over. Close that client before retrying.

### Import existing CLI history

Use **Import projects** in the welcome wizard on the computer that stores your
Copilot CLI sessions. Import reads the configured account directory without
starting a provider or taking ownership of a native session. Imported threads
can also be viewed from connected web, desktop and mobile clients; mobile does
not yet offer the import picker.

Copilot imports are immutable, read-only text snapshots. They retain the native
session ID, model and message times, but omit tool activity, attachments and
possibly older messages. Titles fall back to the first prompt when a native rename
is not recorded in the journal. A model withdrawn by the provider is not retained
as the snapshot's selected model. Importing again does not refresh an existing snapshot.
Invalid journals and files changed since discovery are skipped. Stop activity
in the CLI and scan again before retrying an import of a changing session.
Native continuation and copying snapshot context into a new conversation are
not supported: the current SDK cannot guarantee exclusive admission against
another CLI controller. Closing a window or an old activity timestamp does not
establish that ownership was released.
An offline message recovered for a snapshot is returned to the mobile draft with
a read-only explanation, without uploading attachments or starting a provider.

Plan mode uses Copilot's native planning flow. Tool approvals and questions appear
in the thread. Restricted modes ask before tools run; **Auto-accept edits** allows
file changes, and **Full access** allows tool requests without prompting.
Only one-time approval is offered; Copilot's account-wide permission rules remain
under its own control.

Permission answers wait for the native runtime to acknowledge applying the
decision. An unconfirmed answer is not proof that the tool did not run; do not
repeat the action automatically.

Model/tool steps and subagent activity do not end your submitted turn: the root
native session must become idle. Background tasks remain visible independently.
Automatic native compaction is shown in the thread. Explicit manual compaction,
native conversation rollback, and native forks are not exposed by this integration;
portable handoffs remain available.

# Welcome wizard

T3 Code shows a setup flow when you open a new installation. Existing
workspaces skip this flow.

The hosted app at app.t3.codes does not open setup. With no computer connected,
it asks you to sign in to T3 Connect, then to run `npx t3 connect` on your
computer. From home, it adds compatible computers linked to your account and
opens the app.

Close setup while no import is running to go straight to the app. You can connect
computers and agents later from Settings, or open `/welcome` to run setup again.
Direct links, such as Settings, open normally before setup is done.

## Connect your computers

Select one or more computers to set up. If you opened T3 Code directly from a
server or the desktop app, that computer is already connected and selected.
It is identified by its name, which may differ from the device running your
browser.

You can add more computers before continuing:

- **T3 Connect** connects computers that are signed in to your account.
  [Install the CLI](./install.md#command-line) and run `t3 connect` on each
  computer you want to add, then start T3 Code or run `t3 serve` so the
  computer stays available.
- **Add a computer** connects directly to a server on your network or tailnet.
  Start the server with `t3 serve`, then run `t3 pair --tailscale` and paste
  the pairing link. You can also run `t3 serve --host <address>` and use
  `t3 pair` when the server is already reachable on your network.

A computer marked **Client not supported** runs a T3 Code version that cannot
talk to this app. The message under its name says which side to update.

Saved computers and computers discovered through T3 Connect are selected by
default. Uncheck any you do not want to set up; this does not disconnect them.
Continue when your selected computers are connected. Setup checks
agents across the selected computers, then offers project import grouped by computer.

If T3 Code cannot confirm the workspace during startup, the setup flow shows
**Still connecting** instead of opening the app. Select **Reload** to try again.

If T3 Code cannot read your saved settings, it shows **Could not read settings**.
Select **Retry** after storage becomes available. Setup does not replace
unreadable settings with defaults.

## Check your agents

T3 Code checks each selected computer for Claude Code and Codex. If an agent is
not installed or signed in, select its action to open a terminal with the
correct command ready to run. Install uses the vendor's own installer, which
keeps **Update now** working in Settings. Other providers can be enabled in
Settings.

The setup terminal uses the home directory and environment configured for the
selected provider instance. Sensitive values remain redacted in Settings and
terminal metadata while the terminal process can use them.

## Import your projects

T3 Code finds directories that Claude Code, Codex or an enabled Copilot CLI
account has used. Git repositories
are listed first, newest activity on top. When the remote is on GitHub, the
group shows the repository as `owner/name`. Clones with the same remote share
one group. Directories that are not git repositories sit under "Other folders".

The default selection includes git repositories active within the last 30 days
with at least three conversations. Use the checkboxes, or "Select all" and
"Select none", to change the selection. Linked worktrees of bare repositories
can be offered as separate projects. Other linked git worktrees, Codex scratch
directories under `Documents/Codex`, and anything under `Downloads` are not
offered.

A large or malformed history can reach the scan limit. T3 Code keeps the
projects it found and warns when projects or conversations may be missing.

Imported projects include Codex and Claude conversations active within the last
30 days. You can continue those conversations in T3 Code.
Copilot CLI conversations from that period are imported as read-only text
snapshots, not resumable native sessions. They remain viewable on connected
clients, including mobile. See [Copilot CLI history](providers-copilot.md#import-existing-cli-history)
for limitations.

Conversation import is best effort. T3 Code keeps the first user prompt and the
newest remaining visible user and assistant messages, with 200 messages total.
It omits tool activity and attachments. For Codex, it omits generated setup
context only when a canonical user event and a valid shared turn ID identify the
same user turn. Ambiguous legacy or response-only context stays in the imported
conversation so T3 Code does not remove user text. It reads one conversation at
a time and skips files larger than 4 GiB. It also skips a conversation when the
message text and metadata it keeps need more than 32 MiB of memory. Tool output
does not count toward that limit. It ignores malformed records and skips
unreadable or unparseable conversations.

Each import attempt reads up to 100 conversation files and 4 GiB per project,
with up to 100,000 input records. Run import again to continue a large batch.
Completed conversations are not imported again. You can continue without the
remaining history.

You can continue without configuring agents or importing projects, or return to an earlier step
using the setup progress bar. Navigation pauses while an import is running.
